title: Knowing Your Uncertainty -- On the application of LLM in social sciences
abstract: arXiv:2512.05461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being integrated into computational social science research, yet their blackboxed training and designed stochastic elements in inference pose unique challenges for scientific inquiry. This article argues that applying LLMs to social scientific tasks requires explicit assessment of uncertainty -- an expectation long established in both quantitative methodology in the social sciences and machine learning. We introduce a unified framework for evaluating LLM uncertainty based on Hill numbers, a family of diversity measures. By transforming existing uncertainty quantification (UQ) metrics into Hill numbers, the framework provides a common and intuitive scale for interpreting variation in LLM outputs while accommodating different notions of semantic similarity and different sensitivities to output distributions. translated_title: 认识你的不确定性——论大语言模型在社会科学中的应用
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正迅速被整合进计算社会科学研究中，但其黑箱化的训练过程以及推理中内置的随机元素为科学研究带来了独特的挑战。本文主张，将大语言模型应用于社会科学任务时需要对其不确定性进行显式评估——这一要求早已在社会科学的定量方法学和机器学习领域得到确立。我们基于希尔数这一族多样性度量指标，提出了一个评估大语言模型不确定性的统一框架。通过将现有的不确定性量化指标转换为希尔数，该框架为解释大语言模型输出的变异性提供了一个通用且直观的标尺，同时能够兼容不同的语义相似性概念以及对输出分布的不同敏感性。我们通过四个应用展示了该框架如何帮助大语言模型在社会科学中的应用。
tldr: 该论文基于希尔数提出了一个统一的大语言模型不确定性评估框架，将各类不确定性量化指标转换到通用直观的标尺上，从而为在社会科学中可靠地应用大语言模型奠定方法论基础。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified framework based on Hill numbers for evaluating LLM uncertainty, transforming existing uncertainty quantification metrics onto a common and intuitive scale to enable reliable application of LLMs in social science research.
